correctness.rationale: The upper bounds were independently replayed from the actual certificate blob: for \(Q_3\), 4 reachable policy states cover 81 legal response tuples and 6 nonterminal transitions, giving a 3-cop win within 2 rounds; for \(Q_4\), 27 policy states cover 1,790 response tuples and 90 transitions, giving a 4-cop win within 3 rounds. The audit separately solved the lower-bound belief-state games with fewer cops: from the full state, all reachable non-singleton belief states were enumerated (21 for \(Q_3\) with 2 cops and 217 for \(Q_4\) with 3 cops), and the finite reachability attractor contains none of them, so no finite winning strategy exists with fewer cops. This lower-bound replay uses only singleton legal responses, which remain available when the robber may return one or more neighbors. Thus \(\operatorname{dirloc}(Q_3)=3\) and \(\operatorname{dirloc}(Q_4)=4\) follow without trusting the stored verification log or inaccessible source theorem.
risks: The claim is confined to \(Q_3,Q_4\); certificate round bounds are not claimed minimal.
